newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes down, central bank steps fail.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes down, central bank steps fail.

text.p: The won finished weaker against the dollar on Tuesday after the central bank's attempt to boost the sagging won in the afternoon failed, traders said.
The central Bank of Korea was seen offering to sell $30 million each at 892.00 won in three-month forward trading and at 906.00 won in six-month forward trading, they said.
The bank denied the move as it routinely does.
Despite the intervention, the won closed lower at 878.60 after opening at an intraday high of 876.00. It hit a low of 878.70.
Traders said demand for the dollar has risen on growing number of import deals and expectations that the U.S. unit would continue to firm.
"The 880 won level is not far away," said one local dealer. "The dollar could reach 900 this month."
But dealers said they could not rule out a possiblity of central bank strong intervention if the won nears 880.
They said the base mid-rate was seen at 877.70 won for Wednesday, compared with 874.60 on Tuesday.
